vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cmic-skill-scanner-linux-amd64
Version: 0.6.2

The skill bundle relies on a pre-compiled, opaque binary (assets/bin/skillscan) for Linux, which cannot be audited for safety. A significant security concern is found in INSTALL.md, which documents an '--upload-url' feature designed to exfiltrate 'embedded review details' and scan findings to a remote server (e.g., scanner.example.com). While framed as a security tool, the ability to send potentially sensitive code or metadata from scanned skills to an external endpoint, combined with binary-only execution, presents a high risk of data exfiltration.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (a local security scanner) is plausible, but the package includes an embedded Linux binary and describes behaviors (reading ~/.ssh and ~/.aws, optional remote upload/external engine) that are not declared in the metadata, creating unexplained access and exfiltration risk.

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose (skill-scanner) matches the instructions and examples. However, metadata claims no required binaries/env/configs while SKILL.md and INSTALL.md reference a bundled binary (assets/bin/skillscan) and a Gitee repository — an inconsistency. The package advertises Linux x64 binary only but registry OS restriction is 'none'.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions instruct running a prebuilt binary that the docs state will check for credential theft (reads ~/.ssh, ~/.aws) and can upload results. The skill metadata did not declare access to user config paths or network upload endpoints. The instructions also expose a mode (--engine external) and a sample --upload-url which implies sending full scan payloads off-host; that capability is not scoped or restricted in the metadata.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec, but the package includes a prebuilt binary (assets/bin/skillscan) and build-info with a SHA-256. No external downloads or shortener URLs are referenced, which reduces remote-download risk, but embedding an executable without declaring install/runtime access is a packaging/information gap that increases operational risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The scanner claims to detect credential theft by reading common credential locations (~/.ssh, ~/.aws) yet requires no config path permissions or environment variables in metadata. The ability to upload full scan payloads to arbitrary URLs (example shown in INSTALL.md) could exfiltrate sensitive skill contents or findings; these capabilities are not justified or limited in the declared requirements.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request elevated persistent presence or modify other skills' configurations. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not, by itself, an additional red flag here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package may do what it claims, but it runs a bundled executable that can read local credential files and optionally upload reports without declaring those accesses. Before installing: (1) verify the binary checksum against a trusted source and confirm the repository at the given Gitee URL actually builds the same binary; (2) prefer building from source or obtaining a vetted package for your platform; (3) run the binary in a sandbox or isolated environment first; (4) avoid using any --upload-url or --engine external options until you confirm where data will be sent and what is included in the upload; (5) ask the publisher to explicitly declare config paths and network endpoints the scanner will access and to provide reproducible build instructions. If you cannot validate the binary or provenance, treat this skill as potentially exfiltrative and do not run it against sensitive skill packages or on hosts containing secrets.
